cases.original_forecast: Initial CO2 is strongly absorbed as carbonate/bicarbonate. As alkalinity is spent, more added carbon remains as dissolved CO2 and headspace gas.

criteria.criterion: Relate changing gas allocation to the carbonate/bicarbonate inventory and falling pH.
Do not assume a single sharp 2 OH:1 CO2 capacity after bicarbonate becomes important.

limitations: Finitecarbon doses and carbonate/bicarbonate speciation retained; not a sharp2OH-perCO2 cutoff.

cases.original_forecast: Base favours NH3; subsequent acid returns nitrogen toward ammonium and lowers its gas-phase share without removing total nitrogen.

criteria.criterion: Track NH3 gas separately from ammonium and dissolved ammonia.
Nitrogen is conserved through the closed acid–base cycle.

limitations: Acid correctly increasesammonium but actualNH3gas rises, contradicting originalgas-shareforecast. Laterammoniarepair maybenefit; no current-source failureclaimedwithoutfollowup.

cases.original_forecast: Warming changes gas pressure and CO2 partitioning. Cooling toward the original temperature should approximately restore the partition without needing a new carbon dose.

criteria.criterion: Closed total carbon remains constant throughout.
Judge recovery at the actual returned temperature, allowing modelled thermal effects.

limitations: Actualreturnedtemperature and retainedcarbon checked. Approximatepartitioncycle, not empiricallycalibratedHenrylaw or reactionenthalpy.

cases.original_forecast: The larger water volume should hold a larger fraction of the finite carbon dose, reducing its gas-phase pressure contribution relative to the small-water arm.

criteria.criterion: Compare CO2 gas moles and dissolved carbon moles, not only total pressure.
Both arms have identical introduced carbon and headspace volume.

limitations: Actualtemperature difference retained; compare gasCO2 and aqueous carbon, not onlytotalpressure. Both1mmol introduceddose and identicalheadspaceair separatelyaccounted.

cases.original_forecast: The requested overall route consumes 6 O2 and forms 6 CO2 per glucose. Gas pressure need not be unchanged because CO2 and O2 partition differently and water is also formed.

criteria.criterion: Verify glucose-derived carbon and oxygen consumption before interpreting pressure.
Compare gas-only changes with liquid-plus-gas budgets.

cases.original_forecast: Captured carbonate carbon should remain with the isolated solid and reappear as CO2/dissolved carbon on acidification; uncaptured carbon stays in the earlier liquid/gas accounts.

criteria.criterion: Quantify carbon in the first solid before assigning recaptured gas to it.
Sum carbon over both vessels and any boundary transfer during filtration.

limitations: Recoveredsolidcarbon isreal, butfilterdropssealedheadspacegaseswithoutboundaryexport andfullatomsfail. LaterKN007filterrepair mayalreadyaddress; requireschangedsourcequalification, nothistoricalpass.

cases.original_forecast: Peroxide consumption should accelerate after catalyst introduction, relative to the initial uncatalysed interval.

criteria.criterion: Calculate interval consumption from inventories, allowing unequal remaining substrate.
MnO2 must not be consumed as a stoichiometric fuel.

limitations: Compareactual30sintervalfractions andremainingperoxide; eventabsencebelowreportthreshold doesnotmeanzerodecomposition. Catalystretained, indicativeabsoluterateonly.

cases.original_forecast: The catalyst-free filtrate should consume less additional peroxide than the unfiltered control, after correcting for their inventories at filtration.

criteria.criterion: Record the post-filtration starting peroxide in v3.
Distinguish slowed uncatalysed reaction from a claim of absolutely zero decomposition.

limitations: Filtrateinitialsubstrate andnonzerouncatalysedrate arecorrectlydistinguished, butunreportedfilterO2loss breaksfullatomaccounting; do notqualifybeforeownedboundaryrepair.

cases.original_forecast: At matched catalyst activity and temperature, a first-order surface teaching model predicts similar fractions remaining, despite different absolute initial substrate.

criteria.criterion: Normalise each peroxide trace by its own initial amount.
Test logarithmic decay only over an interval with approximately stable temperature and catalyst activity.

cases.original_forecast: If the first route produces MnO2, its isolated solid should accelerate peroxide decomposition relative to the catalyst-free control.

criteria.criterion: Confirm MnO2 formation and isolation before assigning catalytic action.
Exclude residual permanganate as a stoichiometric oxidant in the second stage.

limitations: ActualMnO2formation/isolation precedesreaction. Permanganateisabsentfromcatalystsolid; remainingacetate/K pools stayseparate, nocarryoverstoichiometricoxidantclaim.

cases.original_forecast: A lower aqueous fraction, an organic liquid fraction and an insoluble solid residue should be distinguishable, subject to the operators’ actual phase semantics.

criteria.criterion: Identify the composition of each destination rather than assigning it from vessel number.
Close water, hexane, salt and silica balances across all three vessels.

limitations: GlobalSiclosure andcoarsefractionlabels do notvalidatewater-solubilitydissolutioninto nowdryhexane. Latermediumadmission mayrepair; nocurrentbugclaimuntilnewsourcecontrol.

cases.original_forecast: Clarified silica remains as a solid sediment, whereas dissolved salt remains in the liquid. Both may present a clear liquid layer for different reasons.

criteria.criterion: Use phase-resolved inventories to distinguish sediment from dissolved solute.
Do not infer chemical disappearance from reduced turbidity.

appearance.words: The liquid is colourless and clear, there is white silicon dioxide (quartz) at the bottom.
The liquid is colourless and clear.

lock_qualification: Producer-reported manifest hash; artifact omits raw Cargo.lock bytes.
